messages:
sam: Heads-up team — we're seeing chatter about an imminent public disclosure for CVE-2026-0421 (libcipher). Need quick triage: patch schedule, SLA impact, and disclosure timing.

maria: Any technical details yet? severity / exploitability?

sec-bot: Scanner alert: affected components: hosted runtime v3.1.x, dedicated nodes running runtime v3.0.x. Vulnerability: remote code execution via malformed request parsing. PoC unconfirmed. CVE link internal only.

nate: If RCE is possible, treat hosted as P0. Recommend emergency hotfix for hosted within 6h. Canary -> 10% -> 100% with automatic rollback on errors.

emily: Can we hotpatch or do we need node restarts? Runtime change requires a restart to load patched libs. Rolling restart per node ~2–5m expected; add circuit breaker.

jackie: For Dedicated customers we need to respect maintenance windows and contracts. My proposal: canary in low-traffic region tonight (02:00 UTC), global rollout next morning. Offer SLA credits proactively if we impact latency SLOs.

sam: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers: we should produce backport bundles + upgrade scripts and coordinate with PM/PS for assisted installs. Legal to confirm disclosure windows.

legal-bot: Do not publicly disclose until we hit internal rollout thresholds. Coordinate coordinated disclosure timeline: embargo until 48h after majority-hosted rollout or explicit legal sign-off.

devops-oncall: We'll need a capacity reserve for canary. Suggest reserving a pool of 5 GPUs to isolate canary traffic and avoid cascading impact.

maria: KMS note: patched runtime changes key access path. Need to validate KMS client connection pooling doesn't exceed HSM/KMS limits. Also ensure audit logs capture any key access spikes during rollout.

nate: Also check RBAC surface: patch touches admin endpoints for cache invalidation. Add smoke tests to prevent permission escalation. Example checks: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://runtime.internal/health` and `kubectl rollout status deployment/runtime --watch`.

emily: I've opened a PR with the fix + backport scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287 — includes upgrade guide and automated smoke tests. Running staging tests now.

sam: Decision summary (proposal):
- Hosted: immediate emergency rollout. Canary within 6h, expand to 100% within 24h if no regressions. Auto-fallback enabled.
- Dedicated: canary 02:00 UTC tonight, full rollout next-day morning. Pre-notify affected customers and include SLA mitigation language.
- Private: ship patch bundles + backport instructions; offer assisted upgrade for enterprise customers within 72h.
- Customer tiers: enterprise = P0 (priority assisted upgrade), midmarket = scheduled maintenance, self-serve/PLG = advisory + scripts.

jackie: I'll draft the customer-facing note: short, action-oriented. Example snippet: "We will apply a security patch to address a vulnerability in the runtime. You may see brief latency during canary. Enterprise customers will be contacted directly for assisted upgrades." Add opt-out instructions for on-prem.

maria: Monitoring: add regression evals against our customer prompt sets during canary. If quality regression >2% or error rate spikes, trigger rollback and pause rollout.

sam: Any immediate blockers?

devops-oncall: Need confirmation to lock DB migration window 01:45–02:30 UTC and reserve 5 GPUs. If approved, I'll take actions now.

jackie: Legal wants embargo lifted only after 75% of hosted traffic patched OR after 36h, whichever is later. Keep press hold.

sam: Action items: emily deploy canary to hosted staging (now), devops reserve GPUs & lock migration window, jackie draft comms & legal coordinate embargo, maria run RBAC/KMS smoke tests. Reconvene in 30m in #eng-security. :thumbsup: :eyes:
